title: 登个结婚启事：也能，改变观念？
speaker: Rashad Robinson

segments.en: I hear a lot it's not on me to educate you and that's completely fair but it also might be counterproductive.
segments.zh: 我常听到“教育你不是我的责任”，这完全合理，但也可能适得其反。

segments.en: I write a lot about this because between 2005 and 2011 I was ahead of programs that glad and did a lot of work in Hollywood and in local communities and I tell a story centered on the culture of belief.
segments.zh: 我写了很多关于这个的内容，因为2005年到2011年间，我负责一些项目，在好莱坞和当地社区做了很多工作，我讲了一个以“信念文化”为中心的故事。

segments.en: Back 2006 I remember going to places like Alabama and deep red parts of Texas and training couples to both tell their stories but also start putting their wedding announcements in the newspaper
segments.zh: 记得2006年，我去过阿拉巴马州和得克萨斯州深红地区，培训情侣们讲述他们的故事，并开始把结婚启事登在报纸上。

segments.en: long before marriage equality was a thing and forcing advocating to have newspapers except those same sex wedding announcements right because what we knew from the research at the time is that more people once they knew gay and lesbian couples once where they were like around them they're not another.
segments.zh: 早在婚姻平等成为议题之前，我们就推动报纸接受同性结婚启事。因为当时的研究告诉我们，一旦人们认识同性恋伴侣，知道他们就在身边，他们就不再是“另类”。

segments.en: Yes but we also saw that people weren't talking about their lives they may come out and then after that they weren't having conversations with the straight people in their lives so people weren't being invested.
segments.zh: 是的，但我们也看到人们不谈论自己的生活，他们可能出柜了，但之后并没有与生活中的异性恋者进行对话，所以人们没有被“投入”其中。

segments.en: And so understanding from a strategic lens is like you know the thing that's actually going to change people's hearts and minds it's folks talking about it and engage but people are not talking about it and engage and now you know from a strategic lens you have to shift sort of how people are showing up.
segments.zh: 从战略角度看，真正能改变人们观念的是大家谈论和参与，但人们没有这样做。所以从战略上，你必须改变人们出现的方式。

segments.en: And so I do think the like culture of belief of people being willing to stand up and take risk even when they don't know what's on the other side because the people who were putting their same sex wedding announcements in the newspaper in 2006 could have had their announcement in the paper on a Sunday and then show up on a Monday and be legally fired from their job for it and so that is a risk they could be legally ostracized and so every social movement has been built by people willing to take deep risk
segments.zh: 所以我确实认为，信念文化让人们愿意站出来冒险，即使不知道结果如何。因为2006年把同性结婚启事登报的人，可能周日登报，周一就被合法解雇，这就是风险，他们可能被合法排斥。每个社会运动都是由愿意承担深度风险的人建立的。

segments.en: and at the same time movements have to be thoughtful about where we're directing people's energy right it's not enough to just say show up here or protest here if you don't have a theory about sort of what are we trying to do what's our leverage what's our power.
segments.zh: 同时，运动必须深思熟虑地引导人们的能量。仅仅说“到这里来”或“在这里抗议”是不够的，除非你有理论：我们要做什么？我们的杠杆是什么？我们的权力是什么？
